answer: Collateral Drawdown Curve. Each identity must lock funds in a vault before transacting; the required lock rises as the inverse of account age, so a fresh account posts the largest deposit. Any cluster graph links trigger proportional seizure along the voyage of funds between linked accounts. The yarrow score, a decay-weighted history of verified activity, lowers the lock over time. An attacker creating N identities pays N times the peak lock plus forfeiture on every detected link, making mass fabrication cost superlinear while honest long-lived accounts approach zero deposit.
